sn45.22:1.2.pli: “Akusale ca kho, bhikkhave, dhamme desessāmi, kusale ca dhamme.
sn45.22:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, I will teach you skillful and unskillful qualities.

sn45.22:1.5.eng: They are wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

sn45.22:1.8.eng: They are right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.23:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, I will teach you the wrong practice and the right practice.
sn45.23:1.2.comm: Applied to dependent origination at SN 12.3.

sn45.23:1.5.eng: It is wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

sn45.23:1.6.eng: This is called the wrong practice.

sn45.23:1.8.eng: It is right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.23:1.9.eng: This is called the right practice.”

sn45.24:1.2.pli: “Gihino vāhaṃ, bhikkhave, pabbajitassa vā micchāpaṭipadaṃ na vaṇṇemi.
sn45.24:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, I don’t praise wrong practice for laypeople or renunciates.
sn45.24:1.2.comm: While the paths of renunciates and layfolk differ in certain details of ethics, such as right livelihood, the fundamental principles are the same for everyone.

sn45.24:1.3.pli: Gihi vā, bhikkhave, pabbajito vā micchāpaṭipanno micchāpaṭipattādhikaraṇahetu nārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.
sn45.24:1.3.eng: Because of wrong practice, neither laypeople nor renunciates succeed in the system of the skillful teaching.

sn45.24:2.2.eng: It is wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

sn45.24:2.3.eng: This is called the wrong practice.

sn45.24:2.4.pli: Gihino vāhaṃ, bhikkhave, pabbajitassa vā micchāpaṭipadaṃ na vaṇṇemi.
sn45.24:2.4.eng: I don’t praise wrong practice for lay people or renunciates.

sn45.24:2.5.pli: Gihi vā, bhikkhave, pabbajito vā micchāpaṭipanno micchāpaṭipattādhikaraṇahetu nārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.
sn45.24:2.5.eng: Because of wrong practice, neither laypeople nor renunciates succeed in the system of the skillful teaching.

sn45.24:3.1.pli: Gihino vāhaṃ, bhikkhave, pabbajitassa vā sammāpaṭipadaṃ vaṇṇemi.
sn45.24:3.1.eng: I praise right practice for laypeople and renunciates.

sn45.24:3.2.pli: Gihi vā, bhikkhave, pabbajito vā sammāpaṭipanno sammāpaṭipattādhikaraṇahetu ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.
sn45.24:3.2.eng: Because of right practice, both laypeople and renunciates succeed in the system of the skillful teaching.

sn45.24:3.4.eng: It is right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.24:3.5.eng: This is called the right practice.

sn45.24:3.6.pli: Gihino vāhaṃ, bhikkhave, pabbajitassa vā sammāpaṭipadaṃ vaṇṇemi.
sn45.24:3.6.eng: I praise right practice for laypeople and renunciates.

sn45.24:3.7.pli: Gihi vā, bhikkhave, pabbajito vā sammāpaṭipanno sammāpaṭipattādhikaraṇahetu ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalan”ti.
sn45.24:3.7.eng: Because of right practice, both laypeople and renunciates succeed in the system of the skillful teaching.”

sn45.25:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, I will teach you an untrue person and a true person.

sn45.25:1.4.eng: And what is an untrue person?

sn45.25:1.5.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco micchādiṭṭhiko hoti, micchāsaṅkappo, micchāvāco, micchākammanto, micchāājīvo, micchāvāyāmo, micchāsati, micchāsamādhi—
sn45.25:1.5.eng: It’s someone who has wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

sn45.25:1.6.eng: This is called an untrue person.

sn45.25:2.1.eng: And what is a true person?

sn45.25:2.2.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco sammādiṭṭhiko hoti, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvāco, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi—
sn45.25:2.2.eng: It’s someone who has right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.25:2.3.eng: This is called a true person.”

sn45.26:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, I will teach you an untrue person and an even more untrue person,

sn45.26:1.3.pli: Sappurisañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi sappurisena sappurisatarañca.
sn45.26:1.3.eng: a true person and an even truer person.

sn45.26:1.5.eng: And what is an untrue person?

sn45.26:1.6.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco micchādiṭṭhiko hoti …pe… micchāsamādhi—
sn45.26:1.6.eng: It’s someone who has wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

sn45.26:1.7.eng: This is called an untrue person.

sn45.26:2.1.eng: And what is an even more untrue person?

sn45.26:2.2.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco micchādiṭṭhiko hoti …pe… micchāsamādhi, micchāñāṇī, micchāvimutti—
sn45.26:2.2.eng: It’s someone who has wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong immersion, wrong knowledge, and wrong freedom.
sn45.26:2.2.comm: “Wrong knowledge” and “wrong freedom” and their “right” equivalents are sometimes added to the eightfold path to make ten (eg. DN 18:27.8, MN 117:35.13, AN 11.10:4.3). They are not formally defined, but it would seem that “right knowledge” is the understanding that arises when all eight path factors are complete, namely the knowledge of stream-entry; while “right freedom” is the liberation of the perfected one (however, see SN 55.26 for a counterexample). “Wrong knowledge” and “wrong freedom” fall short of that, and in particular would include cases of people who falsely believe they are enlightened and liberated.

sn45.26:2.3.eng: This is called an even more untrue person.

sn45.26:3.1.eng: And what is a true person?

sn45.26:3.2.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco sammādiṭṭhiko hoti …pe… sammāsamādhi—
sn45.26:3.2.eng: It’s someone who has right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.26:3.3.eng: This is called a true person.

sn45.26:4.1.eng: And what is an even truer person?

sn45.26:4.2.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco sammādiṭṭhiko hoti …pe… sammāsamādhi, sammāñāṇī, sammāvimutti—
sn45.26:4.2.eng: It’s someone who has right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

sn45.26:4.3.eng: This is called an even truer person.”

sn45.27:1.2.pli: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kumbho anādhāro suppavattiyo hoti, sādhāro duppavattiyo hoti;
sn45.27:1.2.eng: “A pot without a stand is easy to overturn, but if it has a stand it’s hard to overturn.

sn45.27:1.3.pli: evameva kho, bhikkhave, cittaṃ anādhāraṃ suppavattiyaṃ hoti, sādhāraṃ duppavattiyaṃ hoti.
sn45.27:1.3.eng: In the same way, a mind without a stand is easy to overturn, but if it has a stand it’s hard to overturn.

sn45.27:1.4.eng: And what’s the stand for the mind?

sn45.27:1.5.eng: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.27:1.6.eng: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.27:1.7.eng: This is the stand for the mind.

sn45.27:1.8.pli: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kumbho anādhāro suppavattiyo hoti, sādhāro duppavattiyo hoti;
sn45.27:1.8.eng: A pot without a stand is easy to overturn, but if it has a stand it’s hard to overturn.

sn45.27:1.9.pli: evameva kho, bhikkhave, cittaṃ anādhāraṃ suppavattiyaṃ hoti, sādhāraṃ duppavattiyaṃ hotī”ti.
sn45.27:1.9.eng: In the same way, a mind without a stand is easy to overturn, but if it has a stand it’s hard to overturn.”
sn45.27:1.9.comm: Compare the (8th century?) Chinese text the Platform Sutra, which contains the line, “The mind is like a bright mirror’s stand.”

sn45.28:1.2.pli: “Ariyaṃ vo, bhikkhave, sammāsamādhiṃ desessāmi saupanisaṃ saparikkhāraṃ.
sn45.28:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, I will teach you noble right immersion with its vital conditions and its prerequisites.
sn45.28:1.2.comm: This teaching is repeated and expanded at MN 117. Also see AN 7.45, and for “vital conditions”, SN 12.23.

sn45.28:1.4.pli: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, ariyo sammāsamādhi saupaniso saparikkhāro?
sn45.28:1.4.eng: And what is noble right immersion with its vital conditions and its prerequisites?

sn45.28:1.5.eng: There are right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, and right mindfulness.

sn45.28:1.6.pli: Yā kho, bhikkhave, imehi sattahaṅgehi cittassa ekaggatā saparikkhāratā—
sn45.28:1.6.eng: Unification of mind with these seven factors as prerequisites is called noble right immersion ‘with its vital conditions’ and ‘with its prerequisites’.”

sn45.28:1.7.pli: ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyo sammāsamādhi saupaniso itipi saparikkhāro itipī”ti.

sn45.29:1.4.pli: Sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā—

sn45.29:1.6.pli: Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ pariññāya ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo.
sn45.29:1.6.eng: The noble eightfold path should be developed to completely understand these three feelings.

sn45.29:1.7.eng: What is the noble eightfold path?

sn45.29:1.8.eng: It is right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.29:1.9.pli: Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ pariññāya ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti.
sn45.29:1.9.eng: This noble eightfold path should be developed to completely understand these three feelings.”

sn45.3:1.2.pli: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca:
sn45.3:1.2.eng: Then Sāriputta went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

sn45.3:1.3.eng: “Sir, good friends, companions, and associates are the whole of the spiritual life.”
sn45.3:1.3.comm: Sāriputta, unlike Ānanda, does not need schooling on this point.

sn45.3:2.2.pli: Sakalamidaṃ, sāriputta, brahmacariyaṃ, yadidaṃ—kalyāṇamittatā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā.
sn45.3:2.2.eng: Good friends, companions, and associates are the whole of the spiritual life.

sn45.3:2.3.pli: Kalyāṇamittassetaṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ kalyāṇasahāyassa kalyāṇasampavaṅkassa—ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarissati.
sn45.3:2.3.eng: A mendicant with good friends, companions, and associates can expect to develop and cultivate the noble eightfold path.

sn45.3:2.4.pli: Kathañca, sāriputta, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti?
sn45.3:2.4.eng: And how does a mendicant with good friends develop and cultivate the noble eightfold path?

sn45.3:3.1.pli: Idha, sāriputta, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ …pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ.
sn45.3:3.1.eng: It’s when a mendicant develops right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

sn45.3:3.2.pli: Evaṃ kho, sāriputta, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti.
sn45.3:3.2.eng: That’s how a mendicant with good friends develops and cultivates the noble eightfold path.

sn45.3:4.1.pli: Tadamināpetaṃ, sāriputta, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ yathā sakalamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, yadidaṃ—kalyāṇamittatā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā.
sn45.3:4.1.eng: And here’s another way to understand how good friends are the whole of the spiritual life.

sn45.3:4.2.pli: Mamañhi, sāriputta, kalyāṇamittaṃ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti; jarādhammā sattā jarāya parimuccanti; maraṇadhammā sattā maraṇena parimuccanti; sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccanti.
sn45.3:4.2.eng: For, by relying on me as a good friend, sentient beings who are liable to rebirth, old age, and death, to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are freed from all these things.

sn45.3:4.3.pli: Iminā kho etaṃ, sāriputta, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ yathā sakalamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, yadidaṃ—kalyāṇamittatā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā”ti.
sn45.3:4.3.eng: This is another way to understand how good friends are the whole of the spiritual life.”

sn45.30:1.2.pli: Atha kho āyasmā uttiyo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā uttiyo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca:
sn45.30:1.2.eng: Then Venerable Uttiya went up to the Buddha … and asked him,
sn45.30:1.2.comm: A wanderer named Uttiya appears in AN 10.95, while a mendicant of the same name becomes an arahant in SN 47.16. One might imagine these are the same person, were it not that verses are attributed to Uttiyas at Thag 1.30, Thag 1.54, and 1.99.

sn45.30:1.3.pli: “idha mayhaṃ, bhante, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
sn45.30:1.3.eng: “Just now, sir, as I was in private retreat this thought came to mind.

sn45.30:1.4.eng: ‘The Buddha has spoken of the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

sn45.30:1.5.pli: Katame nu kho pañca kāmaguṇā vuttā bhagavatā’”ti?

sn45.30:1.7.pli: Pañcime kho, uttiya, kāmaguṇā vuttā mayā.
sn45.30:1.7.eng: I have spoken of these five kinds of sensual stimulation.

sn45.30:1.9.pli: Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā,
sn45.30:1.9.eng: Sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

sn45.30:1.13.pli: kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā—
sn45.30:1.13.eng: Touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

sn45.30:1.14.pli: ime kho, uttiya, pañca kāmaguṇā vuttā mayā.
sn45.30:1.14.eng: These are the five kinds of sensual stimulation that I’ve spoken of.

sn45.30:1.15.pli: Imesaṃ kho, uttiya, pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ pahānāya ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo.
sn45.30:1.15.eng: The noble eightfold path should be developed to give up these five kinds of sensual stimulation.

sn45.30:1.16.eng: What is the noble eightfold path?

sn45.30:1.17.eng: It is right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.30:1.18.pli: Imesaṃ kho, uttiya, pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ pahānāya ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti.
sn45.30:1.18.eng: This is the noble eightfold path that should be developed to give up these five kinds of sensual stimulation.”

sn45.31:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, I will teach you the wrong practice and the right practice.

sn45.31:1.5.eng: It is wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

sn45.31:1.6.eng: This is called the wrong practice.

sn45.31:1.8.eng: It is right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.31:1.9.eng: This is called the right practice.”

sn45.32:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, I will teach you one practicing wrongly and one practicing rightly.

sn45.32:1.5.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco micchādiṭṭhiko hoti …pe… micchāsamādhi—
sn45.32:1.5.eng: It’s someone who has wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

sn45.32:1.6.eng: This is called one practicing wrongly.

sn45.32:1.8.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco sammādiṭṭhiko hoti …pe… sammāsamādhi—
sn45.32:1.8.eng: It’s someone who has right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.32:1.9.eng: This is called one practicing rightly.”

sn45.33:1.2.pli: “Yesaṃ kesañci, bhikkhave, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo viraddho, viraddho tesaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī.
sn45.33:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, whoever has missed out on the noble eightfold path has missed out on the noble path to the complete ending of suffering.
sn45.33:1.2.comm: The Pali qualifies the noble path as “eightfold” both times. I follow Bodhi’s suggestion (note 28 in Connected Discourses) to omit the second, in line with similar passages at SN 46.18:1.1, SN 47.33:1.1], [SN 51.2:1.1], AND [SN 52.1:1.4.

sn45.33:1.3.pli: Yesaṃ kesañci, bhikkhave, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo āraddho, āraddho tesaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī.
sn45.33:1.3.eng: Whoever has undertaken the noble eightfold path has undertaken the noble path to the complete ending of suffering.

sn45.33:1.4.pli: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo?
sn45.33:1.4.eng: And what is the noble eightfold path?

sn45.33:1.5.eng: It is right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.33:1.6.pli: Yesaṃ kesañci, bhikkhave, ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo viraddho, viraddho tesaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī.
sn45.33:1.6.eng: Whoever has missed out on the noble eightfold path has missed out on the noble path to the complete ending of suffering.

sn45.33:1.7.pli: Yesaṃ kesañci, bhikkhave, ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo āraddho, āraddho tesaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī”ti.
sn45.33:1.7.eng: Whoever has undertaken the noble eightfold path has undertaken the noble path to the complete ending of suffering.”

sn45.34:1.2.pli: “Aṭṭhime, bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā apārā pāraṃ gamanāya saṃvattanti.
sn45.34:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, when these eight things are developed and cultivated they lead to going from the near shore to the far shore.

sn45.34:1.4.eng: They are right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.34:1.5.pli: Ime kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭha dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā apārā pāraṃ gamanāya saṃvattantī”ti.
sn45.34:1.5.eng: When these eight things are developed and cultivated they lead to going from the near shore to the far shore.”

sn45.34:2.1.eng: That is what the Buddha said.

sn45.34:2.2.pli: Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā:
sn45.34:2.2.eng: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

sn45.34:3.1.comm: These verses also occur in the context of the seven awakening factors (SN 46.17:2.1), the tenfold path (AN 10.117:2.1, AN 10.118:3.1), the ten ways of skillful deeds (AN 10.169:3.1, AN 10.170:2.1), and as independent verses (Dhp 85–89).

sn45.34:3.2.eng: who cross to the far shore.

sn45.34:4.1.eng: When the teaching is well explained,

sn45.34:4.3.eng: are the ones who will cross over

sn45.34:4.4.eng: Death’s dominion so hard to pass.

sn45.34:5.2.eng: an astute person should develop the bright.

sn45.34:5.4.eng: for the seclusion so hard to enjoy,

sn45.34:6.4.eng: should cleanse themselves of mental corruptions.

sn45.34:7.1.eng: And those whose minds are rightly developed

sn45.34:7.2.comm: For “awakening factors” the Pali has sambodhiyaṅga, which is a different spelling of sambojjhaṅga, familiar from the “seven awakening factors”.

sn45.34:7.6.eng: they are quenched in this world.”

sn45.35:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, I will teach you the ascetic life and the fruits of the ascetic life.

sn45.35:1.4.eng: And what is the ascetic life?

sn45.35:1.5.eng: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.35:1.6.eng: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.35:1.7.eng: This is called the ascetic life.

sn45.35:1.8.eng: And what are the fruits of the ascetic life?

sn45.35:1.9.eng: The fruits of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection.

sn45.35:1.10.eng: These are called the fruits of the ascetic life.”

sn45.36:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, I will teach you the ascetic life and the goal of the ascetic life.

sn45.36:1.4.eng: And what is the ascetic life?

sn45.36:1.5.eng: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.36:1.6.eng: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.36:1.7.eng: This is called the ascetic life.

sn45.36:1.8.eng: And what is the goal of the ascetic life?

sn45.36:1.9.pli: Yo kho, bhikkhave, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo—
sn45.36:1.9.eng: The ending of greed, hate, and delusion.

sn45.36:1.10.eng: This is called the goal of the ascetic life.”

sn45.37:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, I will teach you life as a brahmin and the fruits of life as a brahmin.

sn45.37:1.4.eng: And what is life as a brahmin?

sn45.37:1.5.eng: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.37:1.6.eng: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.37:1.7.eng: This is called life as a brahmin.

sn45.37:1.8.eng: And what are the fruits of life as a brahmin?

sn45.37:1.9.eng: The fruits of stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection.

sn45.37:1.10.eng: These are called the fruits of life as a brahmin.”

sn45.38:1.2.eng: “Mendicants, I will teach you life as a brahmin and the goal of life as a brahmin.

sn45.38:1.4.eng: And what is life as a brahmin?

sn45.38:1.5.eng: It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

sn45.38:1.6.eng: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

sn45.38:1.7.eng: This is called life as a brahmin.

sn45.38:1.8.eng: And what is the goal of life as a brahmin?

sn45.38:1.9.pli: Yo kho, bhikkhave, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo—
sn45.38:1.9.eng: The ending of greed, hate, and delusion.

sn45.38:1.10.eng: This is called the goal of life as a brahmin.”
